## Historical audit — visible chunk only

**Source:** S0153, `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/scene_rsi_pilot/C1/selection/commons_133800864/trajectory.jsonl`. This is chunk 3 of 4; the other chunks and the rendered image are not visible.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Line 20, `execution_result`, step 3, characters [0,92875) | Blender 4.2.10 reports `ok: true`, synchronizes many separately named Box, Ball and Rod objects, completes 16 render samples, and reports saving `final.png` and `scene.blend`. This establishes multiple named scene objects and a technically completed render/save operation, not what the image depicts or whether the geometry is correct. The log also reports updating shaders, camera and lights, but provides no usable assessment of materials, textures, framing or illumination. |
| Line 21, `select`, step 3, characters [0,59) | Step 3 was selected. Selection is not an independent visual or geometric evaluation. |

**Goal and changes.** The supplied metadata gives no task description. A Blender scene render is observable, but any more specific scene goal would be speculation. The visible result does not show the commands or a before/after comparison, so actual modeling changes, part connections and pose cannot be determined. The image path is evidence of a reported output, not evidence of its contents.

**Teacher and exploration.** No teacher input, detection, diagnosis, proposed update, receipt or adoption appears in this chunk. Nor does it show autonomous exploration or the operations leading to step 3. These are visibility limits, not proof that none occurred elsewhere.

**Outcome and lessons.** Technical rendering and saving are reported successful; **formal task outcome and visual correctness remain unknown**. There is insufficient evidence to classify an empty patch, algorithm failure or technical interruption. The transferable distinction is that a successful render and selection do not verify scene fidelity. Task-specific questions—including whether objects form the intended connected parts, have the intended pose and materials, or suffer camera, lighting or render defects—remain unresolved without the goal, scene inspection and visible render.
